cards.title: What a Social Media Manager actually gets paid to do
cards.takeaway: Social media management is running a business's online presence consistently to build trust, community, and real customer sales.
cards.body:
Many shop owners in Port Harcourt or Lagos are busy serving walk-in customers all day — their Instagram goes silent for three months!

A **Social Media Manager (SMM)** takes that load off their shoulders with **five core tasks**:
1. **Planning** (content calendar & strategy)
2. **Creating** (captions, graphics, short videos)
3. **Publishing** (scheduling at the right times)
4. **Engaging** (replying to comments & DMs warmly)
5. **Reporting** (tracking what actually brought enquiries & sales).

cards.title: Picking the right platform for each job
cards.takeaway: TikTok = fast short-video discovery, Instagram = visual shopfront & Reels, Facebook = local communities & ads, LinkedIn = B2B professionals, X = real-time conversation.
cards.body:
Each platform has a distinct strength:
- **TikTok:** Short, fast-moving video for reaching brand-new people quickly.
- **Instagram:** Visual storefront — Reels, carousels, Stories, and DMs for fashion, food, beauty, and lifestyle.
- **Facebook:** Broad local reach, groups, events, and targeted local ads.
- **LinkedIn:** Professional B2B services, corporate training, and careers.
- **X (Twitter):** Fast news, commentary, and customer service.

check.prompt: What are the FIVE core tasks of a professional Social Media Manager?

choices.text: Planning, Creating, Publishing, Engaging, and Reporting
Buying followers, Spamming groups, Guessing passwords, Arguing in comments, Deleting posts
Repairing laptops, Installing Windows, Soldering boards, Printing flyers, Driving delivery bikes
Only posting 'Good morning' once a month

check.hint: Plan the calendar → Create posts → Publish consistently → Engage replies/DMs → Report results!
check.explanation: Spot on! Those five repeatable tasks turn chaotic posting into a reliable business system.

cards.title: Realistic starter pricing & why 'Consistency' wins
cards.takeaway: Consistency means showing up on a reliable schedule so customers know the business is active and trustworthy — and a realistic small-business Starter package starts around ₦20,000+/month.
cards.body:
Two practical business realities:
- **Consistency:** Posting 3 quality times every single week beats posting 10 times in one weekend and vanishing for two months! Consistency tells buyers: *'This shop is open, reliable, and safe to order from.'*
- **Realistic Starter Pricing:** For a small local restaurant or boutique starting out, a sustainable entry **Starter package** is around **₦20,000/month** (charging ₦500 cannot cover your data/time, and ₦500,000 is far above a tiny neighbourhood restaurant's starter budget).

cards.title: Why you NEVER buy fake followers or promise '10,000 followers in 30 days'!
cards.takeaway: Bought bot followers never buy food or clothes, destroy engagement reach, and ruin trust — promise consistent work and real local growth instead!
cards.body:
What if a client says: *'Just buy me 2,000 followers today'* or asks you to guarantee *'10,000 followers in one month'*?

**Say NO politely and firmly:**
1. Fake bot followers **never buy anything**.
2. Because bots never like or comment, the algorithm sees 0% engagement and **buries** the page so even real customers stop seeing posts!
3. Never hold a client's page hostage, never buy bots, and never make fake viral guarantees — promise **consistent output, honest reporting, and steady real-customer enquiries**.

check.prompt: A client says: 'Just buy me 2,000 cheap followers so my restaurant looks big.' What is the right professional response?

choices.text: Buy the bots secretly and charge double
Explain that bought bot accounts never buy meals and kill your reach in the algorithm — build real local customers with consistent Reels and local promos instead
Change their password and lock them out

check.hint: Bots don't eat jollof rice — and dead engagement signals to Instagram that your content isn't worth showing!
check.explanation: 100% right! Protecting a client's account health and focusing on real local buyers is what separates a trusted pro from an amateur.
